examples.comment: min at x* = b/A = 1.5; J(1) = (2/2)*1 - 3*1 = 1 - 3 = -2; checked here at non-optimal x=1 to exercise the identity, not the minimum.
min at x* = b/A = 2; J(2) = (4/2)*4 - 8*2 = 8 - 16 = -8. Substituting x* gives -b^2/(2A) = -64/8 = -8 -- matches.

metadata.domain_framing: math: least-squares / quadratic-form minimisation. The scalar reduction J(x) = (A/2) x^2 - b x is the rank-1 form of (1/2) x^T A x - b^T x. Optimum x* = b/A is the scalar version of A x* = b.
